- When sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -1.00 or 1.00) in recent days, model should reduce forecast slope or avoid upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model tends to overcorrect — cap forecast rise to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 70s after 75s), model should adjust downward more aggressively in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model should not assume trend continuation — allow for volatility or sideways movement.
- Forecast should not assume linear continuation if true outcome shows non-linear corrections (e.g., 74→70→72→70).
- If sentiment history includes 1.00 followed by 0.00, model should expect a pullback — reduce forecast slope or add downward buffer.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts when sentiment shows recent volatility or negative sentiment — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 14-day average.
